question: Using Figure 6B-1 and Section 6B.06, list the main TTC-zone areas in travel order and identify the three components of the activity area.
model_answer: Direct Answer: A TTC zone is typically divided into four areas that road users encounter in this order: (1) the advance warning area, (2) the transition area, (3) the activity area, and (4) the termination area. The activity area — where the work takes place — is comprised of three components: the work space, the traffic space, and the buffer space. All of this is descriptive (Support) material rather than mandatory, recommended, or permitted practice. Standards (mandatory): (none — the cited provisions are Support/informational only) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 6B-1 depicts the four areas in travel order (advance warning area, transition area, activity area, termination area) and labels the activity area's components — the work space set aside for workers and equipment, the traffic space allowing traffic to pass through, and the lateral and longitudinal buffer spaces providing protection. [Image 2] shows the Section 6B.06 text defining the activity area as comprised of the work space, traffic space, and buffer space. [Image 3] shows Section 6B.03, which lists the four areas of a TTC zone and refers to Figure 6B-1. [Image 4] and [Image 5] show related taper and worker-safety text not directly needed for this question. Citations: - Section 6B.03 Support §1 (p.771) - Section 6B.06 Support §1 (p.773) - Section 6B.06 Support §5 (p.773) - Figure 6B-1 (p.772) - Page 814 - Page 812
gold_answer: Advance warning, transition, activity, and termination. The activity area consists of the work space, traffic space, and buffer space.
